messages:
sam: Heads up — hitting a hang when cancelling a streaming call in py SDK v0.24.1 (uvloop). Repro below, happens reliably for me.

sam: Repro (simplified):
```py
# run under uvloop/asyncio, python 3.11
async def worker(client):
    stream = await client.stream("completion", model=\"open-llm\")
    try:
        async for chunk in stream:
            process(chunk)
    finally:
        # this never gets called when task.cancel() races with next chunk
        await stream.aclose()

# in main test harness
task = asyncio.create_task(worker(client))
await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
task.cancel()  # sometimes cancels cleanly, sometimes the event loop spins and sockets stay open
```

anita: Confirmed locally. When it hangs the event loop goes to ~100% on one core and the socket stays in ESTABLISHED for a long time.

maria: Sounds like generator finalizer / aclose path isn't being hit on CancelledError. Two quick notes: (1) SSE/chunked streams expose an AsyncIterator but not an AsyncGenerator with a close method, so explicit aclose() isn't always available via typing. (2) We should expose an async context manager API so `async with client.stream(...) as s:` calls close reliably.

tyler: Filed an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3456 — summary: async stream cancels can leak socket / never run finalizers. Adding @tyler to triage.

dev-bot: Ticket created: DX-8794 (priority: medium)

anita: Quick patch that helped me in local tests: catch CancelledError and call aclose inside the except/finally. Example: 
```py
stream = await client.stream(...)
try:
    async for c in stream:
        ...
except asyncio.CancelledError:
    await stream.aclose()
    raise
finally:
    # defensive if not already closed
    if hasattr(stream, 'aclose'):
        await stream.aclose()
```
This is ugly but reduces leaks.

sam: FWIW this only repros in SSE (chunked) mode for me, not the websocket path. SDK version pinned to 0.24.1-beta.

maria: Action items: (1) add AsyncContextManager wrapper around streaming API, (2) ensure the iterator object implements `aclose()` and that our generated typing surfaces it (AsyncIterator vs AsyncGenerator), (3) add a unit test that cancels during a chunk boundary.

tyler: I'll pick this up — will add a flaky test harness to catch the race and try a patch that ensures `aclose()` is awaited in generator.__anext__ cancels. Targeting a patch release v0.24.2 EOW.

sam: Thanks — please add notes on sample-app onboarding where we currently use naive `async for` examples; want to avoid pushing that pattern as best-practice until fixed. :thumbsup:
